transcript: The other day, I saw a new play called Someone Spectacular. It’s a play about grief. We see a group of six people who, in the unexpected absence of their grief counselor, begin to converse anyway and see where it takes them. Each character is very distinct, though I felt they were somewhat archetypal or a little too on the nose, but what I found unexpected about this play was just how funny a lot of the dialogue was. It’s heightened but not unbelievable, and I think there's a nice balance between the heightened emotions and dramatic tension you'd hope a play delivers and the somewhat mundaneness of the situation. It really is just six people in a room together for 90 minutes working through the losses they've endured. Should go without saying, but there's some heavy stuff in this one. Someone Spectacular is currently running at Signature through September 7th. With that, another playbill for my collection.
